summary: Defines an abstract model for a presence and instant messaging system, including the entities involved, the terminology, and the services provided. This is an informational memo.

eli5.summary: This is a picture of how chat apps show who is online and pass notes between people.

questions: what is the presence and instant messaging model
how does instant messaging presence work
what is the difference between a fetcher and a subscriber
what are the three s's of presence and instant messaging
subtitle: A shared vocabulary of entities and services for describing presence and instant messaging systems.

tldr.problem: Presence and instant messaging systems were built in many different ways, and there was no common vocabulary for discussing requirements for protocols and markup.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines an abstract model with a PRESENCE SERVICE and an INSTANT MESSAGE SERVICE, the clients around them (presentities, watchers, senders, inboxes) and the data that flows between them.
tldr.outcome: It is meant to be descriptive and universal, not prescriptive. It gives later protocol work a common set of terms rather than a protocol.

today: RFC 2778 is Informational and the unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It was written as a model to support the IMPP working group's protocol work.

sections.title: Purpose of the Model
sections.content:
A presence and instant messaging system lets users subscribe to each other and be notified of changes in state, and lets users send each other short instant messages. The RFC first builds a model: the entities involved, the basic functions they provide and, most importantly, a vocabulary for discussion.

The model is meant to be descriptive and universal. It should map reasonably onto all systems informally called presence or instant messaging systems. It is not prescriptive and does not aim at interoperability: an element in the model need not appear in an interoperable protocol. Model terms are written in upper case, such as PRESENCE SERVICE, and no lower-case term is a model term.
sections.eli5: Before building a chat system, the authors agreed on names for all the parts, so everyone talks about the same thing.

sections.title: The Presence Service
sections.content:
The PRESENCE SERVICE accepts, stores and distributes PRESENCE INFORMATION. It has two sets of clients. PRESENTITIES provide presence information. WATCHERS receive it.

There are two kinds of watcher. A FETCHER requests the current value of a presentity's presence information, and a special fetcher that does so regularly is a POLLER. A SUBSCRIBER asks to be told about future changes, which arrive as NOTIFICATIONS. The service also keeps WATCHER INFORMATION about who has been watching, and may distribute it to some watchers.

A PRESENCE PROTOCOL carries the interaction between the service, presentities and watchers.
sections.eli5: A presentity is a kid who posts where they are. A watcher is a friend who either peeks now and then or asks to be told when it changes.

sections.title: The Instant Message Service
sections.content:
The INSTANT MESSAGE SERVICE accepts and delivers INSTANT MESSAGES. Its clients are SENDERS, which supply messages, and INSTANT INBOXES, which receive them. Each message is addressed to an INSTANT INBOX ADDRESS, and the service tries to deliver it to the matching inbox.

An INSTANT MESSAGE is a small identifiable unit of data. The RFC deliberately does not define "small", but wants to rule out carrying an arbitrary-length stream labelled as an instant message. An INSTANT MESSAGE PROTOCOL carries the exchanges between the service, senders and inboxes. The service may need authentication of senders or inboxes, and may be built from multiple servers or proxies, or even direct communication between sender and inbox.
sections.eli5: A sender hands a short note to the post office, and the post office puts it in the right mailbox.

sections.title: Presence Information Format
sections.content:
PRESENCE INFORMATION consists of any number of PRESENCE TUPLES. Each tuple has a STATUS marker, an optional COMMUNICATION ADDRESS and optional OTHER PRESENCE MARKUP. A communication address pairs a COMMUNICATION MEANS with a CONTACT ADDRESS. The only means the model defines is INSTANT MESSAGE SERVICE, and the only contact address it defines is an INSTANT INBOX ADDRESS, though telephony with a phone number is given as another possibility.

STATUS has at least two mutually exclusive values that affect instant messages: OPEN, where messages will be accepted, and CLOSED, where they will not. The model allows other status values, single or multiple, that may be meaningful only to people.
sections.eli5: A presence card says whether you are open for chatting and where to send the message.

sections.title: Principals and User Agents
sections.content:
A PRINCIPAL is a person, program or group outside the system that appears to the service as a single actor distinct from all others. How the real world maps to principals is outside the model.

A principal uses the system through user agents: an INBOX USER AGENT, a SENDER USER AGENT, a PRESENCE USER AGENT and a WATCHER USER AGENT. Each is purely a coupling between a principal and a core entity. Implementations will usually combine them. The RFC's examples describe a generic "buddy list" as a presence user agent plus a watcher user agent, and an "instant messenger" as a buddy list plus inbox and sender user agents.
sections.eli5: You are the principal. Your chat app is your helper that talks to the system for you.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The RFC says presence and instant messaging systems must deal with "the three S's": STALKING, SPOOFING and SPAM. STALKING is using presence information to infer someone's whereabouts for malicious or illegal purposes. SPOOFING is a principal improperly imitating another. SPAM is unwanted instant messages.

  • ACCESS RULES, VISIBILITY RULES and WATCHER INFORMATION are intended to deal with stalking.
  • The authentication mentioned for the two services is intended to deal with spoofing.
  • DELIVERY RULES are intended to deal with spam.
sections.eli5: The three dangers are someone following you around, someone pretending to be you, and junk notes. The model has a guard for each.
